questions.q: What governance problem existed before Unity Catalog?
options: Permissions, audit logs, and lineage were set per workspace, with no single answer to who could see a table anywhere
Databricks had no permission system of any kind
Tables could only be queried with Python, never SQL
Workspaces could not connect to cloud storage at all
questions.explain: Before Unity Catalog, governance was workspace-by-workspace; Unity Catalog centralizes it on one metastore so a grant applies everywhere the object is accessible.

questions.q: What is the three-level namespace every Unity Catalog object uses?
options: catalog.schema.table
workspace.database.table
account.region.table
schema.catalog.table
questions.explain: Every governed object is addressed as catalog.schema.table — the catalog being the new top level added above the older database.table style namespace.

options: The workspace UI for browsing, managing, and setting permissions on Unity Catalog objects
A command-line tool for migrating Hive tables
A third-party BI tool that connects to Databricks
The Databricks billing dashboard
questions.explain: Catalog Explorer, opened from Catalog in the workspace sidebar, is where you browse catalogs, schemas, and tables and manage their governance.

questions.q: Besides tables, which of these does a Unity Catalog schema also contain?
options: Views, volumes, functions, and models
Only other schemas, nested indefinitely
Only SQL warehouses
Only notebooks
questions.explain: Per Databricks' own object-hierarchy diagram, a schema can contain tables, views, volumes (non-tabular files), functions, and registered models.

questions.q: How does Catalog Explorer's entity-relationship view build the connections it shows between tables?
options: Automatically, from the tables' declared primary and foreign keys
A human must draw every line manually in a diagramming tool
It imports the diagram from an Excel file
It only works for tables created before 2020
questions.explain: Because governed tables are registered with their keys, Catalog Explorer can automatically surface primary/foreign-key relationships as an ER diagram.
